title: AI Builders Digest
subtitle: Bilingual edition · 双语对照版

intro.text: 今天这批内容的共同点，是 AI 已经从「模型有多强」进入到「系统怎么承受它」的问题。Aaron Levie 讲模型路由和 Fable 监管，Madhu Guru 解释 frontier model 发布为什么永远带着不确定性，Steipete 的 PayPal 验证短信则把 agent 的现实边界讲得很直观。另一条更长的线来自 Biohub：如果 AI 要改变科学，关键不是一个中心化超级模型，而是开放工具、湿实验数据和能被更多人拿走使用的基础设施。

archive.title: 系统承压日报
archive.desc: AI 进入真实工作流后，模型监管、路由基础设施、agent 权限边界和开放科学工具同时成为核心议题。

footerNote: Source: Follow Builders curated daily digest. Rebuilt from the 2026-06-14 source feeds.

sections.title: Regulation and Release Risk / 监管与发布风险
sections.desc: 模型越强，发布就越不像传统软件发布：风险不是一个 bug list，而是一组无法完全穷尽的使用场景。

rewrite: Box CEO Aaron Levie uses the Fable export-control situation as an early preview of what model-layer AI regulation could look like at scale.

His core concern is that every release could become a months-long debate with government over model capabilities, jailbreak risk, and subjective assessments of danger. That would slow AI into the shape of a regulated, backlogged industry.
Levie's preferred line is to regulate dangerous applications of AI wherever possible, rather than making the model release itself the primary choke point.
original: This whole Fable export control situation is actually net positive to regulation discourse. It’s an early peek into what AI regulation would end up looking like at scale when enacted at the model layer instead of the specific application of the AI.
So thus the whole challenge will be that you’re debating with the government, over months and months, with every model release, what these models are actually capable of and what their risks are.
This is why, wherever possible, we should be regulating the applied use of AI.

rewrite: Box CEO Aaron Levie 把 Fable 出口管制事件看成一次预演：如果 AI 监管大规模发生在模型层，会是什么样。
他的核心担心是，每次模型发布都可能变成和政府持续几个月的拉扯：模型到底有什么能力、能不能被 jailbreak、危险程度如何评估。这样 AI 会慢慢变成一个发布堆积、节奏迟缓的强监管行业。
Levie 更倾向的边界是：尽可能监管 AI 的危险应用，而不是把模型发布本身变成主要卡点。
original: 整个 Fable 出口管制事件，对监管讨论反而是净正面。它提前展示了当 AI 监管发生在模型层，而不是具体应用层时，规模化之后会是什么样。
挑战会变成：每一次模型发布，都要和政府花几个月辩论模型到底有什么能力、风险是什么。
所以只要可能，我们应该监管 AI 的应用使用方式。

rewrite: Madhu Guru adds the release-review perspective: launching an LLM is not like shipping normal software, because the thing being shipped is a black box with effectively infinite use cases and failure modes.

Even after evals, red-teaming, checkpoint debates, and early-access testing, partners can still uncover behaviors the lab did not anticipate. The operational goal is not perfect certainty. It is reducing uncertainty enough to launch.
That is a useful frame for why frontier model governance keeps getting harder: capability gains expand both useful applications and misuse surfaces at the same time.
original: Launching an LLM isn't like shipping traditional software - you're making a decision about a black box with effectively infinite use cases and infinite failure modes.
Then early-access partners still uncover behaviors you didn't anticipate.
You can never be 100% certain you've understood a frontier model. You focus on reducing the uncertainty enough to launch.

rewrite: Madhu Guru 补上了模型发布评审视角：发布 LLM 不是发布普通软件，因为你发布的是一个黑箱，它有近乎无限的使用场景，也有近乎无限的失败模式。
即使做了 eval、red-team、checkpoint 对比和 early-access 测试，合作伙伴仍然可能发现实验室没预料到的行为。运营目标不是完美确定，而是把不确定性降到足够可以发布。
这也是理解 frontier model 治理为什么越来越难的好框架：能力每提升一次，有价值的用法和滥用面都会同时扩大。
original: 发布 LLM 不像发布传统软件，你是在决定是否发布一个有近乎无限用途和近乎无限失败模式的黑箱。
然后 early-access partners 仍然会发现你没预料到的行为。
你永远不可能 100% 确定自己已经理解了一个 frontier model。你只能把不确定性降到足够可以发布。

sections.title: The Routing Layer Gets Strategic / 路由层变成战略层
sections.desc: 应用层的下一块价值，不只是会调用模型，而是能根据成本、能力和风险把任务切到合适模型上。

rewrite: Aaron Levie says the model-routing layer is going to increase substantially in value. His three reasons are cost optimization, capability maximization, and risk mitigation.

The practical pattern is clear: use frontier intelligence for planning and review, but route the bulk of the workload to an OSS or cheaper model when that is enough. This is not a benchmark argument. It is an architecture argument for applied AI.
The Fable context makes the risk point sharper: if providers or governments can constrain specific models, routing flexibility becomes business continuity infrastructure.
original: The layer that can route to the best AI model for the particular job is going to increase in value substantially.
Even in the same task you may use frontier intelligence for planning and review of the work, but an OSS or cheaper model for the bulk of the workload.
Ultimately, it’s going to increasingly be a a strategic advantage for the applied AI layer that they can effectively route between models.

rewrite: Aaron Levie 说，模型路由层的价值会大幅上升。他给出的三个理由是：成本优化、能力最大化、风险缓释。
实际模式很清楚：用 frontier intelligence 做规划和复核，但大部分执行工作在够用时交给 OSS 或更便宜的模型。这不是 benchmark 争论，而是 applied AI 的架构问题。
Fable 事件让风险点更尖锐：如果 provider 或政府可能限制某些模型，路由灵活性就会变成业务连续性基础设施。
original: 能把具体任务路由到最佳 AI 模型的那一层，价值会大幅上升。
同一个任务里，你可能用 frontier intelligence 做规划和复核，但用 OSS 或更便宜的模型完成大部分工作。
应用 AI 层能有效在模型之间路由，会越来越成为战略优势。

rewrite: Peter Steinberger captures the agent-permissions problem in one line: he got a PayPal verification text, thought he had been hacked, and then realized it was just Codex signing up for a web service it needed.

The funny version is that agents are becoming weird coworkers. The serious version is that once agents cross from local code into accounts, payments, signups, and identity flows, users need much clearer permission boundaries.
original: Got a PayPal verification text and thought I been hacked, but it was just codex signing up for a web service it needed.

rewrite: Peter Steinberger 用一句话抓住了 agent 权限问题：他收到 PayPal 验证短信，以为自己被黑了，结果发现只是 Codex 在注册它需要的 web service。
轻松一点看，这是 agent 变成了奇怪同事。严肃一点看，一旦 agent 从本地代码跨到账号、支付、注册和身份验证流程，用户就需要更清晰的权限边界。
original: 收到一条 PayPal 验证短信，我以为自己被黑了，结果只是 Codex 在注册它需要的一个 web service。

sections.title: Open-Source Biology as AI Infrastructure / 开源生物学成为 AI 基础设施
sections.desc: Biohub 这条线提醒我们，AI 改造科学不是只靠更大的模型，还要靠能产生新数据的科学方法和能被共享的工具。

cards.authorTag: Biohub with Mark Zuckerberg, Priscilla Chan, and Alex Rives

rewrite: The takeaway: Biohub is trying to pair frontier AI with frontier biology, because biology does not have the internet-scale public data exhaust that language models had. The data has to be created through new scientific methods, wet labs, imaging, sensors, cellular engineering, and shared tools.

Mark Zuckerberg frames open source as the fastest path to impact: Biohub is not claiming it will cure diseases itself, but that it can accelerate the whole scientific field by putting tools in more scientists' hands. Priscilla Chan connects that to rare disease work, where patient communities and long-tail researchers can move problems that normal biotech incentives often ignore.

Alex Rives points to ESM Fold as the concrete proof point: a general protein world model trained on billions of sequences can predict structures, support protein design, and even help design single-chain antibodies without being built specifically for that target. The next frontier is a virtual cell that connects genetic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and phenotype layers.
original: We just wanna give tools to the whole scientific community.
It's not just like there's some factory somewhere that you can pay to produce the data. You actually need to invent new novel scientific approaches.
We folded over 1,100,000,000 proteins and predicted their structures.
We didn't design a model for antibodies. We didn't design a model to be able to bind one particular target. We just designed a model that could understand proteins.

rewrite: 核心 takeaway：Biohub 想把 frontier AI 和 frontier biology 绑在一起，因为生物学不像语言模型那样有互联网规模的公开数据尾气。数据必须靠新的科学方法、湿实验、成像、传感器、细胞工程和共享工具被创造出来。
Mark Zuckerberg 把 open source 解释成最快的影响路径：Biohub 不是说自己要治愈疾病，而是要把工具交到更多科学家手里，让整个科学领域跑得更快。Priscilla Chan 把这件事和罕见病连接起来：患者社区和长尾研究者能推进那些传统 biotech 激励机制常常忽略的问题。

Alex Rives 给出的具体证据是 ESM Fold：一个用数十亿蛋白序列训练出来的通用 protein world model，可以预测结构、支持蛋白设计，甚至帮助设计 single-chain antibodies，而不是为某一个特定 target 定制的模型。下一站是 virtual cell，把 genetic、transcriptomic、proteomic 和 phenotype 层连起来。
original: 我们只是想把工具交给整个科学共同体。
这不是某个地方有一个工厂，你付钱就能生产数据。你真的需要发明新的科学方法。
我们折叠了超过 11 亿个蛋白，并预测了它们的结构。
我们没有为 antibody 设计一个模型，也没有为绑定某个特定 target 设计一个模型。我们只是设计了一个能理解蛋白的模型。

sections.title: Old Maps Are Breaking / 旧地图正在失效
sections.desc: 几条短内容都在讲同一件事：AI 市场里的旧判断标准正在失灵，新的信号需要从真实使用里长出来。

rewrite: YC CEO Garry Tan says most people in AI are still using old maps on new territory. His prescription is blunt: throw the maps away and draw new ones by walking the land.

The useful read is not motivational. It is operational. Product form, distribution, margins, and user behavior are all shifting, so copying the last software cycle is a poor substitute for direct contact with the new terrain.
original: In AI most people are still trying to use old maps on a new territory.
Throw the maps away. It's time to draw new ones. The only way you can do it is walking the land.

rewrite: YC CEO Garry Tan 说，AI 里大多数人还在用旧地图看新领土。他的建议很直接：把地图扔掉，亲自走一遍，然后画新的。
这句话有用的地方不是鸡血，而是操作层。产品形态、分发方式、利润结构和用户行为都在变，照搬上一轮软件周期，替代不了对新地形的直接接触。
original: 在 AI 里，大多数人还在用旧地图看新领土。
把地图扔掉。现在该画新地图了。唯一的方法是亲自走这片土地。

rewrite: Garry Tan also makes a quieter point about model discourse: he wishes more people judged a model by actually using it, but most people learn about it through signifiers instead of the thing itself.
That is a good warning for builders and investors. In a hype-heavy market, secondhand symbols travel faster than firsthand product experience, but the latter is still where real judgment comes from.
original: I wish the significance of the model came from more people actually using it and coming to their own conclusions
But yes most people in the world learn about it through signifiers and not through interacting with that which is signified

rewrite: Garry Tan 还讲了一个更安静但更重要的点：他希望更多人通过真实使用模型来判断它的意义，但大多数人其实是通过各种 signifier 认识它，而不是直接和模型互动。
这对 builder 和投资人都是提醒。在高噪音市场里，二手符号传播得比一手产品体验更快，但真正的判断力还是来自后者。
original: 我希望一个模型的重要性，来自更多人真正使用它并得出自己的结论。
但确实，世界上大多数人是通过 signifier 认识它，而不是直接和被指代的东西互动。

rewrite: Nikunj Kothari gives founders a useful market-signal warning: paid partnerships and boosted X views are now negative signals in VC group chats.
The sharper subtext is that artificial traction is starting to backfire. He hopes the same skepticism reaches inflated ARR soon, though he thinks that may take another cycle.
original: Not sure which founder needs to hear this..
but paid partnerships and boosting “views” on X are now negative signal in all VC group chats.
I’m hoping this comes to the inflating ARR trend soon, but that might still take another cycle.

rewrite: Nikunj Kothari 给 founder 一个很实用的市场信号提醒：paid partnerships 和在 X 上 boost views，现在已经是 VC 群聊里的负面信号。
更尖锐的潜台词是，人造 traction 开始反噬了。他希望这种怀疑也尽快落到 inflated ARR 上，只是可能还要再等一个周期。
original: 不知道哪个 founder 需要听到这个。
但 paid partnerships 和在 X 上 boost views，现在已经是所有 VC 群聊里的负面信号。
我希望这种趋势很快也轮到 inflated ARR，但可能还要再等一个周期。

sections.title: Operational Friction Still Matters / 运营摩擦仍然重要
sections.desc: 再强的 AI 工具也会落进日历、安全、流程和团队协作这些朴素系统里，摩擦不会自动消失。

rewrite: Swyx is asking people to fill out the annual AI Engineering Survey, but the more interesting detail is that he had Devin analyze the registered attendee list and output a live chart of who is coming to the conference.

He calls it the best data-driven storytelling he has seen about the community gathering in two weeks. It is a small but useful example of agents turning messy operational data into narrative, not just code.
original: Last chance to fill out the annual AI Engineering Survey this weekend and win great Vercel + Notion + AIE tix!
we had @devinai analyze registered attendee list and output a live chart of the people coming to the conference.
it ended up being the single best data driven storytelling i've ever seen on what kind of community we are gathering in two weeks.

rewrite: Swyx 在提醒大家填写 annual AI Engineering Survey，但更有意思的细节是，他让 Devin 分析已注册参会者名单，并输出了一张展示参会人群的 live chart。
他说这是他见过最好的 data-driven storytelling，用来说明两周后这个社群到底聚集了什么样的人。这是一个小但有用的例子：agent 不只是写代码，也可以把杂乱运营数据变成叙事。
original: 这个周末是填写 annual AI Engineering Survey 的最后机会。
我们让 Devin 分析注册参会名单，并输出了一张参会者 live chart。
结果它成了我见过最好的 data-driven storytelling，用来说明两周后我们聚集的是怎样一个社群。

rewrite: Nan Yu jokes that if software can freeze tech companies and render them worthless, import restrictions should start with Jira.
It works because it points at a builder truth: not all productivity risk comes from powerful models. Sometimes the thing slowing the company down is the process software everyone already normalized.
original: Imagine a piece of software so powerful it completely disables the operations of tech companies, freezing progress and rendering them worthless. Such damaging capabilities must be controlled and stopped.
Import restrictions on Jira. Now.

rewrite: Nan Yu 开了个很准的玩笑：如果有一种软件强大到能让科技公司运转停摆、进展冻结、价值归零，那进口限制应该先从 Jira 开始。
这个笑话成立，是因为它戳中了 builder 的真实经验：生产力风险不全来自强模型。有时候拖慢公司的，就是大家已经习惯了的流程软件。
original: 想象一种软件，强大到可以彻底让科技公司的运营瘫痪，冻结进展，让它们变得毫无价值。这种破坏性能力必须被控制和阻止。
现在就限制 Jira 进口。
